title: Just-in-time elevation procedures for critical ops and post-access audit
creator: Asha Patel
description: Add an auditable, timeboxed just-in-time (JIT) elevation flow for critical operational tasks that require temporary admin privileges. The flow must integrate with SSO/SAML for identity and approval, mint short-lived admin tokens from the privileged broker, and emit high-fidelity audit events to the security SIEM. This ticket defines the request/approval UX, the broker token lifecycle, automatic de-escalation, post-access attestation, and retention/forwarding rules for logs. Goal: eliminate standing emergency credentials while ensuring fast, auditable access for oncall and incident responders.
acceptance_criteria: Users can request JIT elevation via Console and a standardized API; requests require SSO-authenticated identity and at least one approver for P0 operations
Broker issues short-lived admin tokens (<= 15 minutes) scoped to the minimum set of APIs/roles required; tokens are single-use and revoked on session end
All session start/stop events and a command-level audit (API calls) are sent to Splunk/Datadog with retention tag and immutable checksum
Automated de-escalation enforces token expiry and a watchdog revokes tokens after 15 minutes if no heartbeat
Post-access attestation form must be submitted within 24 hours or the user's account is auto-notified and audit shows missing attestation
PagerDuty/Slack approval integration exists and failure/fallbacks are documented in the runbook
Security review sign-off obtained and the feature gate can be enabled per org/team in Console
tasks: Design approval UX in Console (single approver flow + escalation) - DESIGN: Create mockups and accessibility notes
Implement privileged-broker endpoints for mint/revoke and heartbeat
Integrate SSO/SAML assertion verification and require MFA for P0 elevation
Wire audit event schema and forwarding to SIEM (Splunk index: security_privileged_sessions)
Implement post-access attestation API and UI
Add monitoring/alerting for long-lived privileged sessions (>20 minutes) and missing attestation
Write runbook for oncall responders and SOC investigators
Create end-to-end tests and CI that simulate approval, token issuance, and revocation
design_decisions: Use a broker model (separate short-lived token issuer) to avoid embedding emergency keys in services
Require SSO identity + MFA for elevation; do not allow email-only approvals
Record API call metadata rather than full keystroke/session video to balance privacy and forensic needs; allow opt-in session recording for sensitive tenants
Retention default set to 365 days for privileged-session logs; configurable by enterprise customers
Approve-by-slack is supported as an accelerator but must follow SSO mapping to a unique approver identity
Post-access attestation enforced (soft -> hard) to encourage documentation of reason and impact
risks_and_mitigations: Race condition: approval arrives after token minted. Mitigation: broker delays activation until explicit approval event and issues single-use token with activation flag
Privacy: command-level audit may capture secrets. Mitigation: implement automatic redaction rules and a redaction review workflow
Availability: broker outage prevents elevation. Mitigation: documented emergency fallback path with multi-person escalation and time-limited emergency tokens stored in hardware escrow
Abuse: stolen session hijack. Mitigation: require heartbeat from user agent and bind token to ephemeral session fingerprint and SSO assertion
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): enable JIT for infra and SRE teams behind a feature flag and monitor adoption and false positives (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (internal + select customers): invite early enterprise customers to opt-in, gather feedback on attestation UX (3 weeks)
Phase 3 (GA): enable default for all orgs with admin opt-out and documentation and runbook published
Post-GA: collect metrics on mean time to elevation, number of escalations, and audit volume to tune retention/cost
testing_plan: Unit tests for broker mint/revoke and heartbeat logic
E2E test: user requests elevation -> approver approves -> token active -> API call authorized -> token expires -> audit events validated
Load test: simulate 500 concurrent elevation flows and verify latency SLOs for broker minting (<200ms under load)
Security test: red-team scenario for token replay and session hijack attempts

notes: This ticket intentionally avoids creating any permanent emergency credentials. Any exception must be documented and rotated weekly. For air-gapped/private deployments we will provide an HSM-backed escrow flow documented under the Private deployment playbook.
